info.title: AccessHarvester — extract Access DB metadata and translate into a JSON knowledge base.
info.description: Dabbler Access Harvester CLI. Harvests Microsoft Access (.accdb/.mdb) metadata — forms, reports, queries, macros, ribbons, tables, modules — into structured JSON a downstream AI can interpret and document. The extract/run/report-baseline subcommands are COM-based and require Windows + Microsoft Access; parse/translate/generate-docs/validate/generate-migration are file-to-file and run anywhere the .NET 10 runtime does.

options.name: --in
options.description: Path to the Access database (.accdb / .mdb).

options.name: --out
options.description:
Output directory; classification.json is written to
<out>/<database-slug>/classification.json.

options.name: --json-status
options.description: Emit a JSON summary to stdout (human text on stderr).

options.name: --types
options.description:
Comma-separated category filter. Valid categories:
Forms, Reports, Macros, ModulesAndClasses,
Queries, Tables, Relationships, Navigation
Default: all. An unknown value (or a filter that
selects nothing) is a usage error (exit 1), not a
silent empty success.

options.name: --no-clean
options.description:
Skip the default per-tier clean. By default `run`/`extract`/`translate`
delete the target tier directory (raw/ for extract, kb/ for translate,
raw+kb+ir for run) before writing, so a re-harvest of a database whose
source objects have been removed does not leave orphan files behind.
Pass --no-clean to merge-overwrite the prior output in place (the
legacy file-by-file overwrite behaviour); orphan files from objects
removed since the prior run will remain.
IMPORTANT: --types combined with the default clean deletes the entire
tier directory before writing, INCLUDING previously-harvested
unselected categories. For example, `run --types Forms` against an
existing output tree clears raw/, kb/, and ir/ wholesale and then
repopulates only Forms-related content; Reports / Queries / Tables
etc. from prior runs disappear. To do an incremental partial re-harvest
that preserves prior categories, pass --no-clean alongside --types.

options.name: --include-pdf
options.description:
(report-baseline only) Also render each successfully aggregated
report to output.pdf via DoCmd.OutputTo, into the non-gated
reports-baseline-spot-check/ sibling (NOT the byte-diffed corpus).
Off by default: the default capture is the deterministic
aggregates.json alone. The PDF is a non-deterministic binary
intended for human visual review only and never enters the
regression gate; a render failure is non-blocking and recorded on
spot-check-manifest.json without affecting the report's gated status.

options.name: --json-status
options.description:
Emit a JSON summary to stdout at end (human messages go to stderr).
For run/extract/translate the envelope carries provenance fields:
HarvesterVersion (deterministic), StartedAt (UTC ISO-8601,
non-deterministic), DurationMs (non-deterministic), Clean (the
effective per-tier clean mode for this invocation).

options.name: --out
options.description:
Output directory; schema.sql, data.sql, and a
migration-manifest.json are written to <out>/<database-slug>/.

options.name: --in
options.description:
Harvested output root (the directory containing ir/, e.g. a
`run` --out root's AccessMetaData/<dbName>/ — or the ir/
directory itself). ir/Tables + ir/Relationships are the schema source.

options.name: --classification
options.description:
Reviewed classification.json (schema v1.0). Supplies multi-value /
preserve decisions; optional but recommended.

options.name: --data
options.description:
The `sanitize` subcommand's CSV-per-table output directory
(<sanitize-out>/<database-slug>/). Optional: when omitted, schema.sql
is still emitted and every table is flagged as missing data.

options.name: --json-status
options.description: Emit a JSON summary to stdout (human text on stderr).

options.name: --in
options.description: Root directory produced by `run` or `translate` (contains ir/ subdirectory).

options.name: --manifest
options.description: Path to a single manifest.json (output dir is inferred as its parent).

options.name: --harvest-date
options.description: Calendar date anchoring the date-signal threshold (YYYY-MM-DD; default: today).

options.name: --threshold-days
options.description: Date-signal threshold in days, integer >= 1 (default: 90).

options.name: --no-com
options.description: Skip COM date sampling; rely on DAO LastUpdated fallback.

options.name: --json-status
options.description: Emit a JSON summary to stdout.
